docRequirement: how-claude-code-works.md:74 binds auto-memory loading to two limits at once: "The first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever comes first, load at the start of each session." memory.md:384 restates it and adds the consequence — "Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start" — and sub-agents.md:522 repeats the same "first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md` ... whichever comes first" for a subagent's memory directory. Both limits must apply to every MEMORY.md layer, and whichever is hit first must truncate the load.
current: Only the line half exists, and only on a composer the live route never reaches. `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8) is applied by `readMemoryFile` (memory-store.ts:29-33) as a pure line slice — `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — with no byte accounting; `readMemoryFileWithImports` (memory-store.ts:66-110) threads the same `maxLines` per imported file and `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (memory-store.ts:317-334) merges the layers. But `loadMemoryPromptBlock` has exactly one production caller, prompts/system.ts:453-455, and it is gated `capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`. Both live backends pass `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` for that argument (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6607, packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1256), which is true on every normal turn, so the 200-line composer is the legacy fallback only. On the pinned route each MEMORY.md layer is discovered as a capability record by `memoryFileRecords` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:369-434; entry points at :909 global `~/.nessy/MEMORY.md`, :978 session MEMORY.md, :1027 `.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md`, :1092 project MEMORY.md), projected as a `memory` layer with no size field (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:968-978), read WHOLE by `readText` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:169-186 — `readFileSync(contentPath)` then `content.toString('utf-8')`, no cap), and pushed verbatim into the pinned block by `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:976-1014; the read is at :977, the only transform at :1003-1007 is dropping `@import` lines) which `buildPinnedCapabilityContext` (base-agent.ts:884-905) returns for delivery. No byte cap exists anywhere on this path: `grep -rna "read limit\|memory-index\|over its read" packages` returns nothing, and the only instruction-content byte cap in the repo is `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024` (native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :872-877), which covers lazily-read nested CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md files, never MEMORY.md.
divergence: Two deltas, not one. (1) The 25KB limit is absent from the entire repo — there is no byte constant, no byte accounting, and no truncation on any memory path; the value is missing, not misnamed. (2) The 200-line limit exists but is unreachable on the live route: `readMemoryFile` is reached only from the legacy composer (memory-store.ts:77 via prompts/system.ts:455, taken only when `capabilityContextPinned` is false) and from the import-discovery scan at native-sources.ts:427; the pinned route reads the same files uncapped through materializer.ts:169-186. Net observable behaviour on a normal turn: a MEMORY.md of any length and any byte size loads in full, so BOTH documented limits are unenforced where it matters, while the codebase still reads as if the line limit were live.

change.what: Add `export const MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024;` beside MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT:8. Extract the truncation into a pure exported helper so the pinned route can reuse it on already-read text: `export function applyMemoryLoadLimits(text: string, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT, maxBytes = MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT): string` — walk `text.split(/\r?\n/)`, stop when `out.length >= maxLines`, and stop before a line whose `Buffer.byteLength(line,'utf8') + (out.length ? 1 : 0)` would push the running total past `maxBytes`, then `out.join('\n').trim()`. Cutting on a line boundary keeps 'whichever comes first' honest and never splits a multi-byte character. Rewrite `readMemoryFile` (:29-33) to `existsSync` guard + `applyMemoryLoadLimits(readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8'), maxLines)`; keep the existing `(filePath, maxLines)` signature so `readMemoryFileWithImports` (:68, :77, :100) is untouched.

One-line-scale fix at the memory-layer read, :976-1014. After `const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)` (:977), for layers that are NOT rules (`layer.format !== 'rule'` — the same discriminator :984 already uses; `format` is set only for rule files, resolver.ts:975) pass the text through `applyMemoryLoadLimits` before it reaches :997 `const body = ...` . Do it before the `@import`-strip at :1003-1007 so the cap is measured against the file as written, matching the legacy composer. Leave `format === 'rule'` layers uncapped: the 200/25KB rule is spelled for `MEMORY.md`, and rule bodies have their own path-scoped load semantics.

Add the byte half beside it: a MEMORY.md of ~50 lines each ~1KB must come back at or under 25 * 1024 bytes and must end on a whole line; and a 250-line file of short lines must still stop at 200 lines (existing assertion, proving 'whichever comes first' cuts on the line limit when bytes are under budget). One multi-byte (non-ASCII) case to prove no character is split.

There is no test anywhere that asserts the pinned block's text — `grep -rlan "capability-layer" packages --include="*.ts"` matches base-agent.ts only. Add one that drives `composePinnedCapabilityContext` with an oversized MEMORY.md memory layer and asserts the emitted `<capability-layer>` body is capped, which is the assertion that would have caught this.

blastRadius: Two readers of the shared helper, and one of them is not a prompt. (1) `readMemoryFile` is called at packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:427 to scan a MEMORY.md for `@import` lines during capability DISCOVERY. Adding a byte cap there changes which imported files become `memory` capability RECORDS, which changes `view.memory` membership, the resolver generation key (resolver.ts:968-978), the Sources surface, and the `InstructionsLoaded` eager file list base-agent.ts:1009-1014/:1043-1046 emits — so the cap is not purely cosmetic at that call site; if the discovery scan should stay uncapped, call it as `readMemoryFile(path, MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT, Infinity)` explicitly and say why. (2) The pinned block text rides the cached turn prefix (base-agent.ts:884-905, delivery confirmed at `notePinnedCapabilityContextDelivered` :937): changing it invalidates the prompt cache once per user and shifts the `InstructionsLoaded` set when a file truncates to empty (:1002 `if (body === undefined) continue`, :1008 `if (!withoutImports) continue`). Both live backends consume it — pi-agent.ts:6586-6608 and claude-agent.ts:1244-1257 — so this is a cross-backend behaviour change. Existing tests to re-run: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts, packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/native-sources.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-fork-memory.test.ts (it asserts the pinned/legacy gate). No wire or persisted-schema field changes — capability records store `contentHash` of the FILE, not of the loaded slice, so the snapshot boundary is untouched; but capability-record membership is a generation input, which is the persistence-adjacent risk to name in the plan.
userImpact: Observable today, on every turn. A user whose MEMORY.md has grown past the documented limits gets the whole file injected into the pinned capability block instead of the first 200 lines / 25KB: a 400-line MEMORY.md loads all 400 lines, a 1 MB one loads 1 MB. They see it as unexplained context consumption and token cost that Claude Code would not charge them — and on a small-context gateway model (the default coder model) a large auto-memory index can push a turn into a context-length failure with no message pointing at MEMORY.md. The inverse is also user-visible in a subtler way: the model quotes and acts on memory content past line 200 that the documentation says is dropped, so behaviour that a user tuned against Claude Code's truncation does not reproduce here.

Doc lines re-curled 2026-08-02: how-claude-code-works.md:74, memory.md:30/384/386, sub-agents.md:522. Two adjacent requirements deliberately NOT folded into this spec. (a) memory.md:386 — after a write, Claude Code measures MEMORY.md against the 200-line and 25KB read limits, reminds when near one and returns an `errors#memory-index-is-over-its-read-limit` error when over; nothing in this repo does that (`appendMemoryFile`, memory-store.ts:123-133, writes unconditionally, and the grep for the error string is empty). That is a separate finding and a separate fix, though it shares the two constants this spec adds. (b) sub-agents.md:522 — the per-agent memory-directory path is unimplemented end to end per f089/f148, which I did not re-verify here; on my own reading nothing in `composePinnedCapabilityContext` distinguishes a subagent memory directory, so there is nothing there to cap yet. Unverified by measurement: I did not run a packaged build to observe an oversized MEMORY.md in a live prompt; the impact statement is derived from the read path, which I traced completely.
